reason: lkj(2) on rescor: frm()'s MAP is the mode in frmtmb's own correlation chart. NEWS 0.39.0 gives the rule and its reason: the LKJ density is carried onto frmtmb's unconstrained Cholesky parameters with the exact Jacobian of that map, so that on those parameters it means what lkj(eta) means on the correlation matrix; NEWS 0.49.0 extends class rescor to lkj(). Stan's chart differs, so the L1 constant moves 0.40/0.42/0.38 at the three points even with Stan's Jacobian for Lrescor added. Same model, chart-dependent MAP. rescorpp overlap.

gen_extreme_value mixture: the translator has no rule for brms's tmp_xi, so L1 cannot be built; brms's maximum from 6 optimizing starts is 2.12 nats BELOW frmtmb's, so brms's optimizer, not frmtmb, is the side that did not reach the optimum or the models differ, and the two cannot be told apart without a map; a flat-prior posterior of a mixture is multimodal (run 1: Rhat 2.78).

t2() x rescor: the translator fails on the multivariate t2() block, and L4 does not resolve a penalized model: max |z| 0.545 here against 0.851 for the univariate y1 ~ t2(x, z) control, which is an L1 identity (dev/equiv-variant.R with dev/equiv-variant-p048.R, seed 48). rescorpp overlap.

asym_laplace x gr(cov = A): the value agrees at all three points (constants -1.7e-08, -1.7e-05 and 0, inside the 1e-6 * |ours| tolerance, though the stepped point's constant is about 1e8 times a clean identity's); the gradient check (3.56) does not apply, because the asymmetric Laplace likelihood has kinks at y = mu and its maximum sits on one, where the gradient need not vanish (frmtmb warns of false convergence for the same reason).

sratio mixture with cs(): no translation rule (subscript out of bounds), and the optimizing route leaves frmtmb's maximum 0.81 nats below brms's best of 6 starts (2 converged); a mixture likelihood is multimodal, so a local optimum and a model difference cannot be told apart without a map.

nbinom1 x nl: the table says refused (nl needs a single-mu family), and frm() fits it; the nl x family sweep (dev/equiv-nl-sweep.R) finds the nl fit's logLik equal to the linear fit's. brms has no nbinom1.

von_mises x mi(): frmtmb refuses an mi() response outside gaussian and student; brms 2.23.0 builds and compiles it (dev/equiv-repro-refusals.R). NEWS 0.16.0 states the limit ("imputation models must be gaussian or student") but gives no reason for it, so under the survey's decision standard it is a defect, not a divergence by decision. The row already says refused.

nl = TRUE with an ordinal family fits the thresholds alone and drops the nonlinear body without a word: logLik -267.12 equals the intercept-only fit, against -255.52 for the same predictor written linearly and brms's maximum -255.52 (rstan::optimizing, 6 starts). Same for sratio, cratio, acat and cumulative, with or without thres() (dev/equiv-repro-thresnl.R, seed 49). The table says nl x cumulative is refused; frm() does not refuse.

frm_curve() (and frm_linpred(type = "link")) on an ordinal fit with cs() return the shared predictor eta alone; brms's posterior_linpred() at the same parameter values returns eta + cs_k per threshold, and frmtmb's own fitted(scale = "linear") already matches brms to every digit (dev/equiv-repro-cscurve.R, seed 13). The model itself is an L1 identity.

frm(importance = 200) stops with "did not converge ... the corrected negative log-likelihood ROSE" on poisson y ~ x + (1 + x | g), 10 groups of 20; the Laplace fit is an L1 identity with brms (constant -1.9e-10 at the estimate; dev/equiv-variant.R with dev/equiv-variant-laplace.R). Draw-count sensitivity in dev/equiv-repro-importance.R: 512 draws fit.

frm(importance = 200) stops with "did not converge" on binomial y | trials(10) ~ x + (1 | g), 10 groups of 20, the textbook case the option exists for; it also stops at 512 draws and at 512 draws with 20 rounds, and fits at 1000 (logLik -418.11188 against quadrature's exact -418.11209 and Laplace's -418.12333; dev/equiv-repro-importance.R, seed 124). The Laplace fit is an L1 identity with brms (constant 8.0e-13; dev/equiv-variant.R with dev/equiv-variant-laplace.R).

brms's class = "sds" prior on s(x) is refused by name; brms 2.23.0 builds and compiles the model (dev/equiv-repro-refusals.R). frmtmb's own spelling, class = "sd" with group = "s(x)", is the same model: against brms's sds prior it is an L1 identity, constant -0.667 at all three points, gradient 1.6e-13 (dev/equiv-variant.R with dev/equiv-variant-d2.R; the review measured the same). The fix is an alias of sds to that spelling.

fcor() x nl, spelled as brms takes it, bf(..., nl = TRUE, autocor = ~ fcor(M)): brms 2.23.0 builds and compiles it; frm() refuses ("Residual correlation terms are not supported in a nonlinear formula"). The reason is only in a compat note, which the survey's decision standard does not count, so this is a defect. The first spelling put fcor(M) in the nl body, which brms also fails on.

poisson x arma(cov = TRUE): brms 2.23.0 builds and compiles the latent-residual model; frm() refuses (a residual correlation needs a family with a real residual). The reason is only in a compat note, so under the survey's decision standard this is a defect. Under cov = FALSE, the first spelling, brms refuses the MA part as well.
